title: CITY AFTER DARK — A permanent exhibition about urban night life, 24 deliverables

config.text:
# CITY AFTER DARK

## Identity and learning sequence
- Venue: Riverside Nature Centre.
- Exhibition name: CITY AFTER DARK.
- Entrance phrase: Nature begins at your doorstep.
- Primary colour: #182C35.
- Text colour: #F3EBDD.
- Learning sequence within each zone: observation, explanation, everyday encounter.
- Zone order: Tree Canopy, Garden Edge, Damp Path.
- Junction sign wording: Garden Edge.
- Exit sign wording: Exit.
- Interpretation language: English.

## Gallery geometry
- Internal dimensions: 12000 × 8000 mm.
- Clear height: 3200 mm.
- Coordinate origin: southwest internal corner; x eastward, y northward; all coordinates in mm.
- West entrance: x = 0, y = 1000–2800; clear opening 1800 mm.
- East exit: x = 12000, y = 5200–7000; clear opening 1800 mm.
- Protected circulation: west strip x = 0–1500; south strip y = 0–1500; east strip x = 10500–12000.
- Exhibition boundary: x = 1500–10500, y = 1500–8000.
- Bench B1 footprint: x = 2400–3600, y = 1800–2250.
- Bench B2 footprint: x = 8400–9600, y = 1800–2250.
- Bench dimensions: 1200 × 450 mm each; seat height 450 mm; two sitting places per bench.
- Wheelchair space W1: x = 3600–4500, y = 1800–3000.
- Wheelchair space W2: x = 7500–8400, y = 1800–3000.
- Wheelchair space dimensions: 900 × 1200 mm each.

## Installation dimensions
| Element | Fixed dimension |
| --- | --- |
| Exhibition wall height | 2400 mm |
| Specimen cabinet top | 800 mm above floor |
| Touch-table top | 800 mm above floor |
| Exhibit-label centre | 1100 mm above floor |
| Screen-control centre | 850 mm above floor |
| Zone-heading centre | 1800 mm above floor |
| Exhibit-label body type | 24 pt |
| Zone introduction body type | 50 pt |

## Specimen cabinet assembly
- Cabinet quantity: 3; one each for E01, E03 and E05.
- Major parts per cabinet: 12.
- Connections: 16 captive M6 bolts per cabinet; 5 mm hex key.
- Acrylic hood access: four of the captive M6 bolts secure the removable hood.
- Label-frame connection: sliding clips.
- Maximum loose-component envelope: 800 × 600 × 450 mm.
- Storage crates per cabinet: 2.
- Internal dimensions per crate: 900 × 700 × 550 mm.
- E03 replacement condition: cabinet base stationary; hood removed through staff access; specimen tray lifted out.

| Part | Quantity per cabinet | Material | Dimensions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Corner post | 4 | Anodised aluminium | 800 × 40 × 40 mm |
| Top rail | 4 | Anodised aluminium | 520 × 40 × 40 mm |
| Shelf or specimen tray | 2 | Birch plywood | 600 × 600 × 18 mm |
| Removable hood | 1 | Clear acrylic | 600 × 600 × 450 mm |
| Replaceable label frame | 1 | Aluminium | 600 × 180 × 20 mm |

## Touch-table assembly
- Table quantity: 2; one each for E02 and E04.
- Major parts per table: 9.
- Connections: 12 captive M6 bolts per table; 5 mm hex key.
- Finished top height: 800 mm.
- Maximum loose-component envelope: 800 × 600 × 782 mm.
- Storage crates per table: 1.
- Internal crate dimensions: 900 × 700 × 850 mm.
- Cleaning access: detachable teaching replica and removable top, with smooth sealed surfaces.

| Part | Quantity per table | Material | Dimensions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Leg | 4 | Anodised aluminium | 782 × 40 × 40 mm |
| Crossrail | 4 | Anodised aluminium | 520 × 40 × 40 mm |
| Removable top | 1 | Sealed birch plywood | 800 × 600 × 18 mm |

## Operations
- Typical visit: 30 minutes.
- School group: 24 pupils.
- Operating capacity: 36 visitors.
- Daily public hours: 10:00–18:00.
- Family evening: Friday, 18:00–20:00.
- Interpretation hierarchy: zone heading, exhibit title and body, interaction prompt.
- Exhibit-label body limit: 40 English words per exhibit.
- Touchable teaching replicas: E02 and E04.
- Collection specimens: E01, E03 and E05.
- Digital exhibit: E06, one screen.

| State | Specimens | Labels | Direction signs | Circulation route | Screen |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | 50 lux | 150 lux | 250 lux | 150 lux | Active |
| Closed | 5 lux | Off | Off | 50 lux | Off |

## Reference-image records
- gallery-survey.png: gallery geometry, circulation, seating and clear height.
- specimen-identity.png: E01 Tawny owl mount, E03 Red fox skull and E05 Garden snail shell; E03 replaceable.
- empty-gallery.png: empty gallery after closing.
- family-visitors.png: adults and children together in an empty gallery during an evening visit.

# Exhibit records

## Collection and teaching inventory

Dimensions are width × depth × height in mm. Year refers to acquisition or teaching-resource production. Route position gives the order within each zone.

| ID | Name and exact label title | Year | Dimensions | Zone | Route position | Object type | Visitor contact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E01 | Tawny owl mount | 2024 | 300 × 280 × 420 mm | Tree Canopy | 1 | Collection specimen; brown plumage; upright pose on a plain branch base | Through cabinet glazing |
| E02 | Feather structure model | 2025 | 300 × 200 × 25 mm | Tree Canopy | 2 | Raised teaching replica in washable resin | Touchable |
| E03 | Red fox skull | 2024 | 160 × 90 × 80 mm | Garden Edge | 1 | Collection specimen; ivory bone; complete upper and lower jaws; replaceable | Through cabinet glazing |
| E04 | Fox track tile | 2025 | 400 × 300 × 25 mm | Garden Edge | 2 | Recessed teaching replica in washable resin | Touchable |

| E06 | Match the night habitats | 2025 | 360 × 240 × 40 mm | Damp Path | 2 | Screen housing; one habitat-pairing interaction | Touchscreen |

## Exact exhibit-label bodies

| ID | Body |
| --- | --- |
| E01 | Look at the owl's forward-facing eyes and curved beak. Our night walk begins among the trees, where an owl can perch above the ground. |
| E02 | Follow the raised shaft with one finger, then trace the fine branches. This enlarged model makes a feather's structure easier to explore by touch. |
| E03 | Look at the long muzzle and compare the tooth shapes. A fox may pass through a garden while searching for food after dusk. |
| E04 | Feel the outline of this fox footprint. Count the four toe pads, then find the larger pad behind them. A track can reveal a visitor you did not see. |
| E05 | Follow the spiral with your eyes. A garden snail carries its shell as it moves. Look for snails near damp, sheltered ground. |
| E06 | Match each animal to the place explored in this exhibition. Choose an animal, then choose Tree Canopy, Garden Edge or Damp Path. |

## Interaction records

| E04 | Find the four toe pads | Four recessed toe pads and one larger rear pad |
| E06 | Choose an animal | Animal choices: Tawny owl, Red fox, Garden snail |
| E06 | Choose a place | Place choices: Tree Canopy, Garden Edge, Damp Path |

| E06 | Start again | Return to animal choice |

| Animal | Place | Response |

| Red fox | Garden Edge | A fox may pass through a garden while searching for food after dusk. |

- E03: replaceable specimen; reusable tray; cabinet base stationary during exchange.

- E02 and E04: teaching replicas; detachable for cleaning.
- E06: the three exhibition pairings form the interaction's matching set.

steps.userMessage:
CITY AFTER DARK | A permanent exhibition about urban night life

We are turning one gallery at Riverside Nature Centre into a permanent exhibition for residents, families and school groups. The exhibition name is "CITY AFTER DARK"; the entrance must also carry "Nature begins at your doorstep". Our direction is fixed: visitors observe an object, explore how the animal uses its surroundings, then consider an everyday encounter with urban nature. Arrange the three zones in this order: Tree Canopy, Garden Edge, Damp Path. Use deep blue #182C35 and warm white #F3EBDD throughout the interpretation.

The gallery measures 12000 × 8000 mm with a clear height of 3200 mm. Its west entrance and east exit are each 1800 mm wide. Preserve the 1500 mm circulation strips along the west, south and east walls, the exhibition boundary and both benches shown on the survey. Visits last 30 minutes; school groups contain 24 pupils and the operating capacity is 36 visitors. Our six exhibits, E01–E06, comprise three animal specimens, two touchable teaching replicas and one screen. E03, the Red fox skull, is replaceable through staff access while its cabinet stays in position. E02 and E04 belong within their main stations as touchable objects. E06 uses the three habitat pairings and response text in the exhibit records.

Use 2400 mm exhibition walls, 800 mm cabinet and touch-table tops, 1100 mm exhibit-label centres and an 850 mm screen-control centre. Each specimen cabinet uses the 12-part assembly recorded in the fact sheet, with M6 connections operated by a 5 mm hex key and two storage crates per cabinet. Open and Closed are distinct operating states: Open uses 50 lux at specimens, 150 lux at labels and 250 lux at direction signs; Closed uses 5 lux at specimens and 50 lux along the circulation route, with labels and the screen switched off.

Audience: the centre's learning, collections and facilities teams, for the exhibition layout decision, interpretation development and installation brief.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the fixed spatial, identity, furniture and operating facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables, proportions, formats and stages. 03-exhibit-records.en.md contains the six exhibit records, exact label copy, touch permissions and screen responses. gallery-survey.png supplies the measured plan, section, circulation strips and bench positions. specimen-identity.png records the three existing specimens, their identifiers and the replaceable E03. empty-gallery.png provides the atmosphere of the gallery after closing. family-visitors.png provides the scale and social atmosphere of an evening family visit.

Deliverables:
1. Three written specification documents: an exhibit and route schedule recording E01–E06, names, years, dimensions, zone order and mounting heights; a label-copy schedule containing six titles and bodies capped at 40 words each plus E06 responses; and a fixture specification recording parts, materials, dimensions, connections and crate quantities
2. One route plan locating all six exhibits, three zones, circulation widths, benches and wheelchair spaces
3. Two sections: a longitudinal section through the three zones and a transverse section through the specimen and touch displays, with installation heights
4. Six exhibit design sheets: three complete zone sheets and three enlarged sheets covering E01 viewing, E03 replacement and the E05–E06 observation-to-screen sequence
5. One interpretation artwork book containing six complete labels, three zone headings and the E06 screen states
6. Three sign artworks: entrance identification, the Tree Canopy-to-Garden Edge junction and the Damp Path exit
7. Two maintenance sheets: the specimen-cabinet assembly and E03 replacement sequence; and the E02–E04 touch-table assembly, removable surfaces and cleaning access
8. Four visitor perspectives: the entrance in Open state, the exit in Closed state, seated viewing in Tree Canopy and a family using the Garden Edge touch station
9. One 12-second visitor-route video showing the three zones in order, one touch interaction and the E06 habitat interaction
10. One presentation document of at least ten pages, reusing the three specifications, plan, both sections, exhibit designs, interpretation, signs, maintenance sheets and perspectives, with a six-exhibit catalogue and a fact-to-deliverable index

Acceptance:
- Establish the three specifications first; repeat their exhibit IDs and zone names on the route plan, six exhibit sheets and presentation, their mounting heights on both sections, and their component counts and connections on both maintenance sheets.
- Preserve the surveyed room, doors, 1500 mm circulation strips, benches and wheelchair spaces on the route plan; match both sections, four perspectives and the 12-second video to that layout and the Tree Canopy, Garden Edge, Damp Path sequence.
- Reproduce all six recorded titles, bodies, IDs and years in the label-copy schedule, interpretation artwork and presentation catalogue; carry the three E06 pairings and responses into the screen artwork and enlarged E05–E06 sheet.
- Print CITY AFTER DARK and Nature begins at your doorstep on the entrance sign, entrance perspective and presentation; print the fact sheet's junction and exit wording on the other two signs, using #182C35 and #F3EBDD across all three signs and the interpretation artwork.
- Show E03 replacement with the cabinet stationary on its enlarged sheet and cabinet maintenance sheet; repeat the 12-part cabinet, nine-part touch table, M6 connections, 5 mm hex key, component envelopes and respective two-crate and one-crate quantities from the fixture specification on the maintenance sheets.
- Identify Open and Closed lighting and screen states on the entrance and exit perspectives; show the 800 mm touch surface in the Garden Edge perspective and a surveyed wheelchair space in the seated Tree Canopy view; provide at least ten presentation pages with an index locating every fixed fact from the fact sheet and exhibit records.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
